title: tokenization-edgecase-probes-lab
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a personal scratchpad exploring tokenization edge cases that cause surprising model outputs or metric drift in prompt libraries. Aim: catalog reproducible failures, quick experimental prompts, and heuristics for robust templates that survive weird character encodings and adversarial/accidental inputs.

Notes to self (high-level):
- Tokenization differences between tokenizer versions (BPE, sentencepiece) can change few-shot alignment; identical visible text -> different token counts.
- Invisible characters (ZWSP, ZWNJ, BOM, RLO) frequently cause splits that shift example boundaries.
- Homoglyphs and combining diacritics can silently change tokens and downstream logits.
- Emojis and long multi-codepoint graphemes blow up token consumption unpredictably.

Quick experimental checklist:
- A: measure token counts for candidate prompts across three tokenizers (tokeA v1, tokeA v2, sentencepiece-lite).
- B: test few-shot separators: "---" vs "\n\n" vs special token (e.g. <|sep|>) with ZWSP injected.
- C: test model completions when examples are split across tokens vs split on codepoint boundaries.

Experiment logs (summary):

1) Zero-width space (U+200B) insertion around separators
Prompt variant: "Example 1:
Q: What is 2+2?
A: 4
​---​
Q: What color is the sky?
A:"
Observed: token counts for second example jump by 3 tokens in tokenizer-v2; model often repeats prior answer instead of switching to new context (likely cache/key-alignment shift).
Actionable hypothesis: avoid invisible chars in assembled few-shot lists; normalize and collapse ZWSP.

2) Right-to-left override (U+202E) accidental paste
Prompt: description block includes a pasted path with RTL override. Model returns an unexpected concatenation and right-to-left text in answer; sometimes sanitizer removes character but tokenization had already consumed a different tokenization boundary.
Note: add strip_nonprintables step in template builder and log sanitized vs raw token counts.

3) Combining characters (accent overlay) to adversarially change a keyword:
Example: replace "not" with "ñot" (n + combining tilde). Visually "not" but tokenized as separate pieces; model treats as different word and occasionally follows inverted predicate.
Mitigation: NFC normalize strings before assembling prompts.

4) Homoglyph substitution for closed-set labels
Few-shot labels: [Yes, No]
Case: replace Latin 'o' with Cyrillic 'о' in one shot. Model sometimes treats labels as different tokens and mis-assigns high-probability run-on completions.
Mitigation: canonicalize label vocab or use numeric labels (1/0) when possible.

5) Long emoji sequences as separators
Prompt uses an emoji line (e.g. "🔥🔥🔥") between examples. Tokenization expands each emoji into 2–4 tokens depending on ZWJ sequences; for high-shot templates this becomes expensive.
Heuristic: replace multi-codepoint emoji separator with ASCII symbol or single reserved token.

6) BOM and file-encoded artifacts in copy/paste
Observed: leading BOM causes first token to be a weird control-character token; some runtimes drop this and others keep it -> mismatch between dev tests and production.
Mitigation: sanitize headers, run UTF-8 validation pipeline.

Mini reproducible cases (to paste into test harness):
- Case A (ZWSP): "Q1: 1+1?
A1: 2​---​
Q2: 3+3?
A2:"  -> inconsistent across tokenizers.
- Case B (Combine): "Label: ñot
Instruction: Choose yes/no." -> check token sequences.
- Case C (RTL): "Path: C:\Users\Alice\Docs\report‮txt
Explain:" -> sanitizer test.

Observed model failure patterns (qualitative):
- Repetition of previous shot when boundary tokenization changes (likely KV cache misalignment).
- Hallucinated label sets when homoglyphs change casing/characters; model invents synonyms.
- Unstable token counts cause bursty billing for long prompt libraries.

Potential experiments to run next (prioritized):
1) Build a small harness that runs 200 permutations of separator characters (ASCII, ZWSP, em dash, emoji) and records top-3 tokenization diffs across three tokenizer versions + per-token cost estimate.
2) Add a sanitizer stage to template library that: normalize (NFC), strip invisible, replace multi-codepoint emoji with single token placeholder, map common homoglyphs to ASCII. Measure delta in model accuracy on 500-shot mixed task.
3) Try using special marker tokens (<EX0>, <EX1>) inserted by code (not visible to user) and removed by client display—does this stabilize completions?

Heuristic rules for prompt-lib (initial draft):
- Always run NFC normalization on user-supplied examples.
- Replace any codepoint in category Cf (format controls) with ASCII space.
- If separator contains emoji-like characters (Emoji property true) convert to reserved placeholder.
- For closed-set labels, use short ASCII tokens (Y/N, 0/1) or map to canonical ids stored externally.

Open questions / risks:
- Do tokenizers change on runtime upgrades (we saw v1->v2 differences)? Need CI gate to pin tokenizer artifacts per model endpoint.
- Are there accessibility/UX tradeoffs when we neutralize visually valid characters? E.g., non-Latin scripts might legitimately use combining marks. Need to whitelist scripts.
- For enterprise/private deployments, sanitize policy might be too aggressive and alter customer data. Provide opt-out.

TODOs and next steps (personal):
- [ ] Implement harness and run 1k permutations next week (track by LIN ticket).
- [ ] Draft a short one-pager for solutions-eng: recommended sanitizer + opt-out pattern.
- [ ] Add unit tests that assert token count invariants for critical templates.

Scratch command snippets (for harness):
- token-count: curl -X POST /tokenize -d '{"text":"..."}' - compare arrays
- sanitize: python -c "import unicodedata; print(unicodedata.normalize('NFC', s))"

Random notes to keep:
- When assembling few-shot by concatenation, prefer injecting explicit numbered markers (Example 1:, Example 2:) — numbers are more robust than punctuation-only separators.
- Keep a small curated list of allowed emoji separators (single-codepoint) if product wants them for UX.

If this becomes stable, fold heuristics into prompt-assembly library and add toggle in Redwood Console to preview sanitized prompt and token delta.

End of scratchpad.
